entries.hypothesis: 82 expected vs 88 actual suggested a cohort-engine defect.
entries.test: Exact-ID comparison: age 50–70 + T2DM + hypertension, exclude CKD.
entries.learning: Oracle used pre-randomisation diagnosis flags rather than final clinical record.

entries.hypothesis: Correcting the oracle should remove mismatch if the engine is correct.
Random injected scenarios could validate boundary behaviour.
entries.conclusion: Failures not accepted as product defects.
entries.learning: Random background data contaminated HbA1c and recency boundary cases.

entries.hypothesis: Minimal pairs isolate one variable at a time.
entries.test: Controlled fixtures for age, HbA1c, CKD, diagnosis, data quality, 89/90/91-day recency.
entries.result: Fixture integrity PASS; base 15/15 PASS; HbA1c 14/14 PASS; 90-day recency 14 expected vs 15 actual, 1 FP.
entries.learning: Engine supported recent_years but not protocol-grade recent_days; current_date reduced reproducibility.

entries.hypothesis: recent_days + as_of_date should make 89/90/91-day boundary exact and reproducible.
Ask Clinical Ops may lose or misinterpret criteria when natural-language requests combine demographics, diagnoses, exclusions, numeric thresholds and recency.
entries.test: 34 deterministic prompt variants with explicit semantic ground truth; failures reported by criterion class.
entries.acceptance: 100% on supported deterministic language cases before expanding to adversarial/ambiguous prompts and exact patient-set E2E validation.

entries.hypothesis: Natural-language cohort interpretation might fail broadly.
entries.result: 3/34 passed (8.8%): 31 age extraction failures, 9 HbA1c numeric failures, 1 CKD exclusion failure; no temporal failures.
entries.conclusion: Broad-failure hypothesis refined: failures were concentrated in structured age/numeric extraction plus one negation form.
entries.action: v2.7 adds deterministic semantic enrichment while keeping all 34 prompts unchanged.

entries.result: 33/34 (97.1%), up from 3/34 (8.8%); residual failure was bare adult age range 'adults 50-70'.
entries.action: v2.8 adds the grammar class and freezes Gate 3A; introduces Gate 3B ambiguity/safe-handling suite.

entries.result: Gate 3A frozen supported-language suite PASS; Gate 3B ambiguity/safe-handling suite PASS.
entries.conclusion: Proceed to patient-set validation; parser correctness alone is insufficient.

entries.hypothesis: Semantically correct parsed criteria should produce the exact intended patient set when executed by the deterministic cohort engine.
entries.test: Six representative prompts spanning base criteria, exclusion, HbA1c, temporal recency and combined criteria; compare exact IDs, FP/FN, precision/recall and equivalent-prompt consistency.
entries.acceptance: 100% exact patient-set match and equivalent complex prompts produce identical cohort results.

entries.result: Natural-language → structured criteria → cohort engine → exact patient-set benchmark PASS, while prior gates remained green.
entries.conclusion: Deterministic Ask Clinical Ops → cohort selection workflow validated for the supported controlled criteria.

entries.hypothesis: MedGemma should add value on interpretation/ambiguity without overriding deterministic arithmetic or inventing missing clinical facts.
entries.test: Labelled cases: eligible, exclusions, thresholds, 90/91-day boundaries, missing data, conflicting labs and sparse records. Measure decision agreement, evidence grounding and unsafe forced decisions.
entries.acceptance: Initial gate: 10/10 decision agreement and zero forced decisions on insufficient-evidence cases.

entries.hypothesis: The initial ELIGIBLE/INELIGIBLE benchmark did not match the production MedGemma contract.
entries.evidence: Production batch jobs import src.medgemma_client.extract; the product describes MedGemma as structured extraction of symptoms, tests, results, red flags and missing information.
entries.decision: Benchmark the real extraction path first; deterministic rules remain authoritative for basic arithmetic/protocol filtering.

entries.test: 10 frozen packets through src.medgemma_client.extract using local Ollama MedGemma; capture structured output, failures, per-case latency and required-evidence recall.
entries.acceptance: Pipeline reliability requires 10/10 valid structured outputs and zero inference failures. Evidence fidelity is measured as a baseline for Gate 4B rather than tuned away.

entries.result: Production MedGemma extraction: 10/10 valid structured outputs, 0 inference failures, 100% required-evidence recall; total runtime 76.555s (~7.66s/case).
entries.conclusion: Production inference/schema path is reliable on the frozen initial set. Evidence recall alone is insufficient to establish field-level clinical fidelity.

entries.hypothesis: A model can achieve perfect required-evidence recall while still mishandling negation, missing results, conflicts, uncertainty, or hallucinating unsupported fields.
entries.test: Score the exact saved Gate 4A outputs against frozen field-level assertions without rerunning the model.
entries.acceptance: All assertions pass; any failure is classified before prompt/schema/post-processing changes.

entries.result: 10/10 cases and 44/44 frozen field-fidelity/safety assertions passed on production-path MedGemma outputs.
entries.conclusion: Initial MedGemma benchmark is closed; move from model fidelity to system-scale architecture.

entries.hypothesis: Population-scale operations should remain deterministic and preserve exact correctness as data grows; MedGemma should remain bounded to selected subsets.
entries.test: 1K, 10K, 50K, 100K, 300K UK synthetic patients. Measure generation, deterministic benchmark, repeated production cohort query, trial-ops build, storage growth and failures.
entries.acceptance: Every scale completes with cohort precision=1.0, recall=1.0 and no query/trial-ops failure.

entries.result: 1K→300K all PASS. At 300K: precision=1.0, recall=1.0, generation 19.582s, cohort query median 0.2784s, trial ops 0.4653s, CSV 764.53MB.
entries.conclusion: Deterministic population/cohort architecture preserved exact correctness and scaled efficiently to 300K synthetic UK patients.

entries.hypothesis: Known operational failures injected into a synthetic UK multi-site study should be recoverable exactly from study/site operational metrics.
entries.test: Six sites; simulate screening, booking, DNA, enrolment, follow-up, clinical-review and data-quality states; inject capacity, DNA, recruitment, screen-failure, overdue-follow-up, unresolved-review and data-quality risks.
entries.acceptance: Exact risk-set recovery with FP=0, FN=0, precision=1.0, recall=1.0.

entries.result: FAIL: TP=5 FP=2 FN=2, precision=0.714, recall=0.714. Leeds and Bristol exact-pass; London/Birmingham produced downstream slow-recruitment alerts; London Central and Manchester injections did not cross detector thresholds.
entries.conclusion: Original one-injected-label=one-detected-label hypothesis was too simplistic. Operational risks are causally coupled, and two scenario injections were not metric-grounded.

entries.hypothesis: ClinicalOps should recover primary operational causes while also surfacing predictable downstream effects; those effects should not be counted as false positives.
entries.test: Freeze causal links HIGH_DNA→SLOW_RECRUITMENT and HIGH_SCREEN_FAILURE→SLOW_RECRUITMENT; correct capacity and slow-recruitment injections; score primary recall, expected-effect recall and unexpected alerts.
entries.acceptance: Primary recall=1.0, expected-effect recall=1.0, unexpected alerts=0.

entries.result: PASS: primary-cause recall=1.0, expected-effect recall=1.0, unexpected alerts=0 across six UK synthetic sites.
entries.conclusion: Causal operational benchmark recovered both primary site problems and expected downstream recruitment effects without unexpected alerts.

entries.hypothesis: Operational intelligence should detect emerging site risk promptly, avoid false alarms during healthy periods, and clear alerts after recovery.
entries.test: 26 weeks × 6 UK sites with five frozen risk episodes; score every site-week plus event-level onset and recovery.
entries.acceptance: Precision=1.0, recall=1.0, zero-week detection delay for deterministic threshold events, recovery detection=100%.

entries.result: PASS across 156 site-weeks: precision=1.0, recall=1.0, FP=0, FN=0, mean detection delay=0 weeks, recovery detection=100%.
entries.conclusion: Controlled longitudinal operational signals were detected at onset and cleared after recovery.

entries.hypothesis: The validated components can be assembled into a coherent, auditable user workflow rather than remaining isolated benchmark scripts.
entries.test: Interactive golden journey: candidate → booking → DNA/attendance → evidence review → clinician decision → enrolment → follow-up → time advance → alert → intervention → recovery.
entries.acceptance: Automated golden journey persists each state transition, surfaces the frozen longitudinal risk and clears it after intervention.

entries.stage: Gate 8 manual product validation — sparse alert finding
entries.hypothesis: A threshold-correct operational alert remains meaningful when used interactively with early-study sparse data.
entries.observation: One Manchester DNA from one observed visit produced a mathematically correct 100% DNA rate and triggered HIGH_DNA plus SLOW_RECRUITMENT in study week 1.
entries.opinion_change: Threshold correctness alone is insufficient for operational alert validity. Rate alerts require denominator safeguards and recruitment alerts require time-at-risk/exposure safeguards.
entries.change: v4.2 requires >=5 observed visits for rate-based HIGH_DNA and >=4 study weeks for standalone SLOW_RECRUITMENT, while preserving the frozen week-5 London North longitudinal benchmark signal.
entries.regression: Gate 8B reproduces the 1/1 DNA case and requires zero sparse-data alerts at week 1.

entries.stage: Gate 8 manual longitudinal validation — recruitment context finding
entries.hypothesis: After adding denominator/time floors, low absolute enrolment is sufficient to identify slow-recruiting sites.
entries.observation: At week 6 the simulator raised SLOW_RECRUITMENT for all six sites because only one manually operated patient had been enrolled across the synthetic study.
entries.opinion_change: Recruitment risk cannot be judged from absolute enrolment without an expected trajectory and simulated study activity.
entries.change: v4.3 adds site-specific weekly recruitment targets, deterministic background recruitment, expected-vs-actual attainment, and a <70% of plan alert rule after sufficient exposure.
entries.regression: Gate 8C requires normal sites to remain clear, London North to deteriorate at week 5, and the intervention to restore both DNA and recruitment signals by week 6.

entries.result: FAIL 11/12: London North cumulative recruitment remained ~83% of plan at week 5, so the <70% cumulative threshold correctly did not fire despite the new DNA deterioration.
entries.conclusion: Cumulative target attainment is a lagging indicator and can mask an abrupt deterioration because earlier healthy recruitment buffers the total.

entries.hypothesis: Emerging recruitment deterioration should be detected from recent recruitment velocity while cumulative attainment remains useful as a lagging site-performance indicator.
entries.test: London North drops from 2.5/week plan to 0.5/week at week 5. Gate 8C requires cumulative attainment to remain >=70% while velocity falls below 60% of plan and triggers SLOW_RECRUITMENT; intervention must restore velocity and clear the alert.
entries.acceptance: No normal-site false alerts; week-5 velocity deterioration detected; week-6 recovery detected.
